params.body:
## Why

Two things broke translated addresses on hoet.be:

- The word in front of the slug was Dutch in every language: `/en/collectie/couture`, `/fr/montuur/o1`. `/en/collection/couture` was a 404.
- Only blog articles remembered their old slugs (`journal_slugs`). A slug changed on a page or a frame in the Studio made the old address a 404, and that old address is the one search engines have indexed. Translated slugs are now being filled in, so this would start happening right away.

A third one showed up while checking: the English slug of the O1 was typed as a sentence (`o1 - 3D printed - titanium - eyewear - couture - round`), and the live sitemap published that address with its spaces.

## What changes

**The word per language** (`config/sanity.php`, `segments`):

| | nl | en | fr | de |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| collection page | collectie | collection | collection | kollektion |
| frame | montuur | frame | monture | fassung |
| blog category | categorie | category | categorie | kategorie |

Every word routes in every language. Whatever comes in that is not the address of this language gets one 301 to it, computed from the document: the old Dutch word, the word or slug of another language, an id address, a former slug, or a combination of these. hreflang, canonical, the language switch, the sitemap, the menu state and the collection tiles all use the new addresses. Pages (`/en/store-locator` and so on) already had translated slugs and keep them. The dealer area (`/bestellen`, behind login, not indexed) and the signed newsletter link keep their paths.

**Slug history for pages and frames** (`App\Support\Slugs`, table `document_slugs`), the same rule as the blog:
- the sync records every slug a published page or frame carries, per language;
- a former slug answers 301 to the current address;
- the slug of a document that is no longer published answers 410; republishing brings it back;
- the newest owner of a slug wins.

The migration fills the table so the first rename after deploy is already covered: from the mirror at migrate time, plus `database/data/document-slugs-2026-11-25.json` (the 200 page and frame slugs published on 2026-11-25), in case a slug changes in the Studio before this deploys. A fresh database starts empty; another brand skips the file.

**Clean slugs and fallback.** `Content::slug()` cleans a slug (`Str::slug`) and treats an empty one as missing, so a language without its own slug uses the Dutch one instead of a 404 or an id. Lookups compare cleaned with cleaned, so the spaced O1 address forwards to `/en/frame/o1-3d-printed-titanium-eyewear-couture-round`.

The old-site list in `PageController` (`couture-brillen` and so on) now resolves through the page and its history, so it also lands in one hop after a rename.

## Checked

- `tests/Feature/LocaleAddressesTest.php` (22 tests): each word per language, the old Dutch word under en/fr/de, the word of another language, per-language slugs, the Dutch fallback, an empty slug, the sentence slug, renamed collection, frame and page slugs (also twice, and old word plus old slug together), old-site addresses after a rename, 410 for unpublished, republish, slug taken over, unknown stays 404, canonical and hreflang, sitemap, and both seed cases. Plus a sync-level test in `SanitySyncTest`.
- Existing tests updated where they asserted the Dutch word under another language.
- Full suite: 456 tests, all green except `BuildStampTest`, which fails only in a git worktree (the ref lives in the shared `.git`) and fails the same on `main`. phpstan 0 errors, pint clean.
- Against a local mirror of the published Hoet content: all 236 URLs in the live sitemap answer 200 (101) or one 301 to a 200 (135). The new sitemap has 236 URLs, all 200, none with a space. No rendered page links to `/en|fr|de/collectie|montuur/`.

## After merge

- The deploy runs the migration; it seeds from the mirror at that moment.
- Search Console: resubmit `/sitemap.xml` so the new addresses are crawled sooner. The 301s carry the old ones over.
- Not in this PR: `http://www.hoet.be` still takes two hops (nginx sends it to `https://www.hoet.be` first). That is the port 80 server block in the Forge nginx config, not this repo.
- The Studio side (field description, slug validation) is a separate PR in hoet-sanity.
params.title: Translated address words and slug history for pages and frames
